description:
WINGMAN PROJECT: Online Combat Multiplayer battles for Starsector (BETA release)

Version 0.9.2-beta  -  for Starsector 0.98a-RC8

DOWNLOAD (GitHub releases)

https://github.com/NEOysod/TheWingmanProject (source)

What is it?

Co-op multiplayer for Starsector battles. One player hosts a battle (a mission, the simulator or a campaign fight) and up to three friends(default, goes up to 16 but why would you do that?) join it, each flying a ship from the host's fleet, side by side, in real time.

Combat only. The campaign stays single-player: the fleet, the cargo and everything won or lost belong to the host.
Joiners fly the host's ships. Pick one in the lobby before the battle, or take the helm of any friendly ship the host allows.
The host is in charge. Only the host gives fleet orders, pauses, and changes the battle speed.
Your own ship answers your controls at once, like single player. Everything else arrives with the connection's delay.

This is a BETA. It has been played mostly by two people. It works, but expect rough edges, and please report what you find (see the bottom of this post).

AI use declaration
This mod was written with the help of AI. Its code and documentation were written with Claude (Anthropic's AI model), used through Claude Code, under my direction. Every change in the project's history is marked as co-written with Claude.

What that means in practice:
I decided what the mod does and how it should behave, reviewed the changes, and tested it in game. Bugs found in playtesting were fed back and fixed the same way.
Claude wrote most of the Java code, the network protocol and its tests, and the guides (README, user guide, technical reference), working from my requests, the Starsector API and the game's own behaviour.
The automated tests (network, data and attack/fuzz tests) are run on every build; what touches the game itself is tested by playing.

No AI-generated art. The mod has no art of its own beyond a mission icon.

The full source is on GitHub, so anyone can read exactly what it does. If something looks wrong, please report it like any other bug.

NEW FOR 0.9.2-beta

fixes bug when accepting refit request from your friends can sometime empty the refit windows.
UI improvement.
tested plenty, still might be bugs anyway.

Host and joiners should both update.

Requirements

Starsector 0.98a-RC8. Host and joiners must run the same game build.
The same mods, in the same versions, as the host. Interface-only "utility" mods may differ. A joiner whose mods differ is refused and shown exactly what differs.
A way for friends to reach the host's PC: the same home network, a virtual LAN (Radmin VPN, Tailscale, ZeroTier, Hamachi), or a port forward. Port 24816 (TCP; UDP on the same port is used too where it gets through, and is optional).

Install

Unzip so the folder is Starsector/mods/Wingman.
Enable The Wingman Project in the launcher.
Start the game. A short how-to opens on the title screen the first time. It's always in the CO-OP panel (top right of the title screen) under F1.

Optional: Wingman's agent (for mods' "player ship" scripts)
You don't need this to play. Without it, everything above works.

On the host, a ship a joiner flies is an AI ship as far as the game knows, so a mod script that does something only for "the player's ship" never does it for a joiner there: fighter take-overs, abilities aimed at the cursor, hotkey abilities (Special Hullmod Upgrades, armaa's repair kit), status lines. The agent fixes that for every mod at once: while the host's game runs a joiner's ship, those scripts treat it as the player's ship, the mouse as the joiner's cursor, and each player uses their own key.

Who should add it: the host matters most. Each player who adds it gets the benefit on their own PC. It changes nothing on disk, and only acts while co-op runs.

How: with the game closed, open the game's launch settings, find -Xms (the memory setting) and put this just before it, followed by a space:

Windows: the file vmparams in the Starsector folder (next to starsector.exe; open it with Notepad):

[/list]-javaagent:..\mods\Wingman\jars\WingmanAgent.jar
[/li]
[li]Linux: in starsector.sh:
-javaagent:./mods/Wingman/jars/WingmanAgent.jar
[/li]
[li]Mac: in the file with the game's -Xms setting: -javaagent: followed by the full path to mods/Wingman/jars/WingmanAgent.jar[/li]

Custom Java launcher (a .bat that runs java.exe @SomeFile.txt, as the newer-Java packs do): vmparams isn't read. Put this on a line of its own at the top of that .txt file instead:
-javaagent:../mods/Wingman/jars/WingmanAgent.jar

If the game won't start and the console says "the system class loader does not define the appendToClassPathForInstrumentation method" (for example with Fast Rendering's setup), remove the -javaagent line and make these three changes in the same file:
add ;../mods/Wingman/jars/WingmanAgent.jar to the end of the -classpath list;
add a line --add-exports=java.instrument/sun.instrument=ALL-UNNAMED (next to the other --add-opens lines);
replace the last line, com.fs.starfarer.StarfarerLauncher, with wingman.agent.Launch.

Check it works: starsector.log says "Wingman agent: running" when the game starts, and "Wingman agent: on" when a co-op battle starts. "not started" means the setting isn't being read. If you renamed the mod folder, use your folder's name instead of Wingman. To turn it off, delete the line again. If the game won't start after adding it, remove it and please report your Starsector version and OS.

How to play

Hosting
Open the CO-OP panel on the title screen and give friends one of the addresses listed there (for Radmin, the one starting with 26).
Set a password (F3 in the CO-OP panel, "Join password") if anyone else can reach your PC.
Load your save. Friends can connect while you are still on the campaign map: they see your fleet and pick the ship they want, and their picks show in your campaign messages.
Start any battle. A picked ship that you deploy is that friend's at once. After you deploy, a ready check holds the battle until everyone has chosen a ship and pressed ready. Enter starts it; Ctrl+Enter starts without waiting.

Joining
Click CO-OP on the title screen, type the host's address, your name and the password (if any), and press Enter. You stay connected for the whole session.
The lobby fills the screen: the host's fleet with a card for each ship, who is here and what they picked. Up/Down and F pick your ship; Delete drops your pick; Tab shows the last battle's report.
Stay in the lobby. When the host's battle begins you are taken into it after a short countdown.
Step 1, choose your ship: if the host deployed the ship you picked, you are already in it. Otherwise Up/Down and Enter or F take one, or W watches without a ship.
Step 2, ready: Enter for ready; Backspace goes back to step 1.
When the battle ends you go straight back to the lobby, still connected, with the host's report of the battle, and join the next one the same way.

In the battle, and keys
Every player has a number and colour: the host is P1 (green), then P2 (blue), P3 (yellow), P4 (white), shown next to each player's ship. F3 hides and shows the tags.
Change ship with the game's Transfer Command on a friendly ship. U hands your ship to the AI and back.
Leave with your ship by giving it the Retreat order, or at the bottom edge of the map with Enter.
If a player drops, the battle pauses and their ship goes back to the AI. Their game reconnects by itself.

Who Key What it does
Anyone, title screen CO-OP, then F1 / F2 / F3 How-to / mod compatibility report / settings
Anyone, battle or campaign map Ctrl+Shift+O Settings
Anyone, battle F3 Hide / show player tags
Joiner, lobby Up / Down, F, Delete, Tab Choose, pick, drop the pick, last battle's report
Host, battle Enter / Ctrl+Enter Start after the ready check / start without waiting
Host, battle Ctrl+Shift+2-9 Remove that player (by their P number)
Host, battle Ctrl+Shift+T Take back the ship you have targeted

Everything can be changed in game (F3 in the CO-OP panel, or Ctrl+Shift+O). Nothing needs editing by hand.

How it works (short version)

The host's game runs the only real battle. Every joiner sees a live copy of it, kept in step many times a second: ships, fighters and missiles (position, hull, armor, flux, shields, systems, weapon aim and fire, ammo), the battlefield (map, backdrop, nebula, asteroids, objectives, wrecks, fleet orders), and every ship's officer and skills. Mod content runs on every copy on the host's timing: weapon, missile, ship system and hull mod scripts, special on-hit effects, and battle objectives added by mods.

Updates carry only what changed, compressed, and go by UDP where possible (TCP takes over by itself where UDP is blocked). If one part of the mod hits an error, that part switches itself off for the battle with a "Co-op:" message, and the game keeps running.

Mod compatibility
Most mods just work: ships, weapons, hull mods, ship systems and missiles from mods are copied like vanilla ones. What causes trouble isn't a mod's size but what its combat scripts assume: a joiner's battle is a copy started from the title screen, with no campaign loaded.

F2 in the CO-OP panel shows the mod compatibility report: what scripted content your mods bring and how each kind is handled. "Worth a look" marks the items to mention in a report.
Battle objectives from mods (Secrets of the Frontier's emplacements and reinforcement beacons, Extra Combat Objectives) appear for everyone.
MagicLib subsystems (extra abilities on their own keys, used by UAF and many other mods) follow the joiner who flies the ship.
Carriers own their fighters on every screen, so carrier scripts (UAF's Rafflesya Control and Isenoria) find them.
If a mod's ship system or objective crashes a joiner's game, it is no longer mirrored on that PC from the next launch (F5 in the CO-OP panel switches it all back on).
Optional: Wingman's agent lets mods' "player ship" scripts (fighter take-overs, cursor-aimed abilities) work for every player's ship. It's one setting in the game's launch settings; see section 9 of the user guide.

Optional: Wingman's agent (for mods' "player ship" scripts)
You don't need this to play. Without it, everything above works.

On the host, a ship a joiner flies is an AI ship as far as the game knows, so a mod script that does something only for "the player's ship" never does it for a joiner there: fighter take-overs, abilities aimed at the cursor, hotkey abilities (Special Hullmod Upgrades, armaa's repair kit), status lines. The agent fixes that for every mod at once: while the host's game runs a joiner's ship, those scripts treat it as the player's ship, the mouse as the joiner's cursor, and each player uses their own key.

Who should add it: the host matters most. Each player who adds it gets the benefit on their own PC. It changes nothing on disk, and only acts while co-op runs.

How: with the game closed, open the game's launch settings, find -Xms (the memory setting) and put this just before it, followed by a space:

Windows: the file vmparams in the Starsector folder (next to starsector.exe; open it with Notepad):

-javaagent:..\mods\Wingman\jars\WingmanAgent.jar
[/li]
[li]Linux: in starsector.sh:
-javaagent:./mods/Wingman/jars/WingmanAgent.jar
[/li]
[li]Mac: in the file with the game's -Xms setting: -javaagent: followed by the full path to mods/Wingman/jars/WingmanAgent.jar[/li]

Custom Java launcher (a .bat that runs java.exe @SomeFile.txt, as the newer-Java packs do): vmparams isn't read. Put this on a line of its own at the top of that .txt file instead:

If the game won't start and the console says "the system class loader does not define the appendToClassPathForInstrumentation method" (for example with Fast Rendering's setup), remove the -javaagent line and make these three changes in the same file:
add ;../mods/Wingman/jars/WingmanAgent.jar to the end of the -classpath list;
add a line --add-exports=java.instrument/sun.instrument=ALL-UNNAMED (next to the other --add-opens lines);
replace the last line, com.fs.starfarer.StarfarerLauncher, with wingman.agent.Launch.

Check it works: starsector.log says "Wingman agent: running" when the game starts, and "Wingman agent: on" when a co-op battle starts. "not started" means the setting isn't being read. If you renamed the mod folder, use your folder's name instead of Wingman. To turn it off, delete the line again. If the game won't start after adding it, remove it and please report your Starsector version and OS.

Known limits
Mostly tested with two players, much of it on one PC. Four players over the internet is the design target, and the least tested.
Effects drawn directly by mod scripts (particles, sounds, arcs) can be a few frames early or late compared with the host.
Phase "bullet time": a battle has one clock, the host's. Joiners don't get the slowdown when they phase; when the host phases, the battle slows for everyone.
Starting the battle from the CO-OP panel relies on game internals of 0.98a-RC8. If a game update breaks it, the mission Wingman: Join Game still works.

Reporting problems

Please do! Turn on "Detailed log" in the settings on both PCs, reproduce the problem, and post (or send me) both starsector.log files, with a line on what happened and your mod list. The F2 compatibility report is worth a screenshot too.

Coming next: friend refits. While the host is docked at a market, joiners will be able to refit the ship they picked and send it to the host to accept or deny.

The full player's guide (hosting, joining, every setting, firewall and troubleshooting) is docs/USER_GUIDE.md in the download.

Have fun flying together!

Joiners fly selected ships from the host's fleet in real-time combat, syncing ship status, weapons, and battlefield elements.
